reading.body:
This record is an unverified OpenStreetMap point in Italy, not a confirmed data center, and it carries no power figure at all.

The only substantive fact is a name, iZOOM.it, and a tag, telecom=data_center. The name embeds a national domain suffix, which is a common convention among Italian hosting and domain-registration businesses. That makes a small Italian web-hosting or IT-services operation plausible. It does not make it a data center in the sense that matters for AI, which is a building with a large and contracted electrical load.

The record's own research status is exhausted, meaning no operator website, press coverage, or business registration was confirmed. The zero in the megawatt field is not a measurement of a facility drawing no power. It is the absence of a measurement. Nothing here establishes scale, service offering, or whether the site operates today.

For AI infrastructure, the useful signal is the gap between how facilities get catalogued and what determines whether they can host compute. A map tag records that something exists at a coordinate. It says nothing about interconnection, cooling, or the power contract that decides whether a building can carry training or inference load. This entry sits entirely on the catalogue side of that gap.

What the data does not tell the reader is anything about capacity, ownership, or grid connection. It also does not tell the reader how many similar unverified points exist in the same source, so it cannot be used to estimate the size of Italy's data center footprint. The nearest airport, Parma at 18.7 miles, is the only other concrete detail, and it is not relevant to compute.
